answer: Each identity registers one inlet catchment, locks a 70 credit bond, and files a reading from its opal float gauge, giving level and window. An auditor recomputes volume from radar, then demands an echo reading; the echo must match within 2 millimetres, and a reused serial or copied reading burns the bond. The first filing costs 32, the k-th 32+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6026 and 1000 fakes pay 3,029,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked. Rented gauges fail: the opal float serial binds to one catchment key, and the echo reading exposes a dead gauge. An honest identity pays 32 once.
